title: Diagnose damaged and misleading backups
goal: Distinguish corrupt streams from incorrect but well-formed payloads.
challenge: Using copies only, distinguish a truncated gzip stream from an altered regular-file payload whose tar listing and gzip stream still pass. Preserve the good backup and trusted expected reference; explain what each check establishes.

steps.command: w=/home/learner/ll-backup-4; test "$(id -un)" = learner && test ! -e "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && mkdir -m 0700 -- "$w" && cd -- "$w" && test "$(df -Pk . | awk 'NR==2 {print $4}')" -ge 65536
steps.explanation: Guard a fresh, learner-owned workspace and check guest free space. Stop if any command fails.
steps.expected: Private practice directory; at least 65536 KiB available.

steps.command: guard() { test "$(pwd -P)" = /home/learner/ll-backup-4 && test ! -L /home/learner/ll-backup-4 && test "$(stat -c %U .)" = learner && test -z "$(find . -type l -print -quit)"; }; guard
steps.explanation: Define and use a location/owner guard for every later change.
steps.expected: Exact physical path, not a link.

steps.command: guard && mkdir -m 0700 source && printf 'alpha\n' > source/note.txt && printf 'bravo\n' > 'source/space name.txt' && chmod 0640 source/note.txt && chmod 0600 'source/space name.txt' && touch -d '2026-01-01 00:00:00 UTC' source/note.txt 'source/space name.txt'
steps.explanation: Create two known regular files, including a name with a space.
steps.expected: alpha and bravo lines, modes640/600, fixed UTC timestamp.

steps.command: guard && test ! -e v1.tar && test ! -L v1.tar && timeout -k 1s 10s tar -cf v1.tar -C source -- note.txt 'space name.txt' && test "$(stat -c %s v1.tar)" -le 65536
guard && sha256sum -- v1.tar > expected-backup.sha256 && cp -- v1.tar altered.tar && printf X | dd of=altered.tar bs=1 seek=512 conv=notrunc status=none
steps.explanation: This trusted GNU tar fixture stores note.txt first; offset512 changes its payload, not its header. Never edit the good backup.
steps.expected: Altered copy has wrong first byte.

steps.command: guard && timeout -k 1s 10s tar -tf altered.tar && timeout -k 1s 10s gzip -c -- altered.tar > altered.tar.gz && timeout -k 1s 10s gzip -t -- altered.tar.gz; sha256sum -- v1.tar altered.tar
steps.explanation: A newly compressed wrong payload has a valid CRC. Readable headers are not content validation.
steps.expected: Listing and gzip check pass; digests differ.

steps.command: guard && cp -- altered.tar.gz truncated.gz && truncate -s -4 truncated.gz; timeout -k 1s 10s gzip -t -- truncated.gz; printf 'gzip status=%s\n' "$?"
steps.explanation: Remove four trailer bytes on another copy only. Nonzero status detects this stream damage.

steps.command: guard && mkdir -m 0700 restore && timeout -k 1s 10s tar -xf altered.tar -C restore --no-same-owner --same-permissions; cmp -- source/note.txt restore/note.txt; printf 'comparison status=%s\n' "$?"; sha256sum -c -- expected-backup.sha256
steps.explanation: Compare restored data to known expectations; the good reference still matches the untouched backup.
steps.expected: cmp nonzero; v1 hash remains OK.

hints: Check the copy, not the retained original.
A CRC checks encoded stream consistency, not whether alpha was intended.
Restore into a separate directory then compare to expected content.
review: Passing altered tar/gzip, failing truncated gzip, differing payload and unchanged good hash.
coverage: LPIC-1 v5.0 103.3 and LPIC-2 v4.5 206.2 partial manual archives/recovery; 104.5 reinforcement where applicable. Self-reviewed, unscored; not complete objectives.
